reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' by absence of any audit right binding the Customer, and the supplied paragraphs support that: none of p0019, p0035, p0084, p0095, p0118 or p0134 grants Garman inspection, examination, entry, usage-reporting or system-access rights.

The two potential hooks are correctly dispositioned: the § 14 reference to 'accounting records for which access is obtained ... pursuant to this Agreement' is definitional and mutual, conditioned on access granted elsewhere (no such grant exists), and § 17(b) is a one-off post-termination self-certification by Sparkling with no vendor entry or auditor involvement.

No redline and no counterparty comment is the expected and correct output for a compliant finding; inserting frequency/notice/cost machinery would create a Customer obligation and manufacture a vendor audit right that does not exist, so 'no edit' is the minimal correct action.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is a false signal here — the regex looks for frequency-capping language that is unnecessary where no audit right exists; absence of any audit right is at least as favorable as the preferred position.
Rationale is internally consistent with the quoted text and does not overstate; no directional error detected.
